title: Faithfulness of the simplex generators-and-relations presentation
statement: Let P be the category with objects [n] for n a natural number, generated by the coface maps delta_i and codegeneracy maps sigma_i modulo the six simplex relations (the two adjacent mixed identities are separate relations). Let J:P → Delta send [n] to the finite ordinal {0,...,n}, and the generators to the usual increasing injection omitting i and the usual monotone surjection identifying i with i+1. For any objects a,b of P and arrows f,g:a → b, J(f)=J(g) implies f=g.

source.place: Lemma 14.2.4(c), simplex relations are complete; pure-block proofs in Kerodon 04FQ and 04FT

proof.text: Prove sigma-block injectivity using exists_normal_form_P_sigma. Two words between the same objects have admissible lists with the same length. The evaluation formulas identify the adjacent equal values with membership in each list (mem_isAdmissible_iff), hence equal maps give identical membership. SortedLT.eq_of_mem_iff makes the two increasing lists equal, and their standard words are equal.

Factor each morphism into sigma then delta blocks by exists_P_sigma_P_delta_factorization. Both mapped blocks are epi-mono factorizations of the same simplex map, so their image objects are equal; equality of lengths reflects this to equality of the middle presentation objects. Uniqueness of simplex epi-mono factorizations identifies both mapped blocks: transport to the image object and use image_iota_eq for the two mono maps, then cancel to identify the epi maps.

Construct a degree-raising contravariant order-duality functor D on the presentation, sending delta_i to sigma_i and sigma_i to delta_(i+1). Check its preservation of all six relations, then descend its quiver action through the quotient. By induction on the presentation generators, J(D(f)) is the image of J(f) under Mathlib SimplexCategory.II. Induction on pure-delta words shows their duals are pure-sigma words. Thus equal pure-delta maps have equal duals by the proved pure-sigma injectivity. Apply D once more. The double-dual functor shifts degree by two and maps delta_i to delta_(i+1). Embed [n] by inserting a last and then a first endpoint, a composite of two cofaces and hence a split mono. The delta-delta relation proves that this embedding commutes with every coface; induction proves naturality on every pure-delta word. Cancel it to recover equality of the original coface words. Apply the two pure-block injectivity results to the epi-mono factorizations to conclude arbitrary morphisms are equal. Every step is proved in Lean; no normal-form existence theorem for delta words is assumed.
